#!/usr/bin/env bash

# Generate thumbnails for files using ImageMagick, following Freedesktop spec
# Usage:
#   ./generate-thumbnails-magick.sh --file <path>
#   ./generate-thumbnails-magick.sh --directory <path>

set -e

# Thumbnail sizes mapping
get_thumbnail_size() {
    case "$1" in
        normal) echo 128 ;;
        large) echo 256 ;;
        x-large) echo 512 ;;
        xx-large) echo 1024 ;;
        *) echo 128 ;;
    esac
}

usage() {
    echo "Usage: $0 --file <path> | --directory <path>"
    exit 1
}

md5() {
    # Calculate md5 hash of the file's absolute path
    echo -n "$1" | md5sum | awk '{print $1}'
}

urlencode() {
    # Percent-encode a string for use in a URI, but do not encode slashes
    local str="$1"
    local encoded=""
    local c
    for ((i=0; i<${#str}; i++)); do
        c="${str:$i:1}"
        case "$c" in
            [a-zA-Z0-9.~_-]|/|'('|')'|'*') encoded+="$c" ;;
            *) printf -v hex '%%%02X' "'${c}'"; encoded+="$hex" ;;
        esac
    done
    echo "$encoded"
}

generate_thumbnail() {
    local src="$1"
    local abs_path
    abs_path="$(realpath "$src")"
    # Skip files with multiple frames (GIFs, videos, etc.)
    case "${abs_path,,}" in
        *.gif|*.mp4|*.webm|*.mkv|*.avi|*.mov)
            return
            ;;
    esac
    local encoded_path
    encoded_path="$(urlencode "$abs_path")"
    local uri
    uri="file://$encoded_path"
    local hash
    hash="$(md5 "$uri")"
    local out="$CACHE_DIR/$hash.png"
    mkdir -p "$CACHE_DIR"
    if [ -f "$out" ]; then
        return
    fi
    # Hard resource ceiling per-process: even a single huge source image
    # (e.g. an 8K photo) can otherwise balloon MagickCore's pixel cache
    # into gigabytes of RAM. This forces it to spill to disk instead of
    # eating all available memory.
    magick -limit memory 256MiB -limit map 512MiB -limit disk 1GiB \
        "$abs_path" -resize "${THUMBNAIL_SIZE}x${THUMBNAIL_SIZE}" "$out"
}

# Parse arguments
SIZE_NAME="normal"
MODE=""
TARGET=""
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case "$1" in
        --file|-f)
            MODE="file"
            TARGET="$2"
            shift 2
            ;;
        --directory|-d)
            MODE="dir"
            TARGET="$2"
            shift 2
            ;;
        --size|-s)
            SIZE_NAME="$2"
            shift 2
            ;;
        *)
            usage
            ;;
    esac
    # Only one mode allowed
    [[ -n "$MODE" ]] && break
done

THUMBNAIL_SIZE="$(get_thumbnail_size "$SIZE_NAME")"
CACHE_DIR="$HOME/.cache/thumbnails/$SIZE_NAME"

if [ -z "$MODE" ] || [ -z "$TARGET" ]; then
    usage
fi

case "$MODE" in
    file)
        if [ ! -f "$TARGET" ]; then
            echo "File not found: $TARGET"
            exit 2
        fi
        generate_thumbnail "$TARGET"
        ;;
    dir)
        if [ ! -d "$TARGET" ]; then
            echo "Directory not found: $TARGET"
            exit 2
        fi
        # Cap how many files we thumbnail in parallel. Without this, a
        # folder with hundreds of wallpapers spawns hundreds of magick
        # processes at once, each holding a full-res image in memory -
        # easily enough to exhaust RAM and crash the system.
        # Fixed at 10 concurrent conversions regardless of core count.
        # Override with THUMBGEN_MAX_JOBS=N if you want to tune it.
        max_jobs="${THUMBGEN_MAX_JOBS:-10}"
        running=0
        for f in "$TARGET"/*; do
            [ -f "$f" ] || continue
            generate_thumbnail "$f" &
            running=$((running + 1))
            if [ "$running" -ge "$max_jobs" ]; then
                wait -n || true
                running=$((running - 1))
            fi
        done
        wait || true
        ;;
    *)
        usage
        ;;
esac

FILE: ./scripts/thumbnails/thumbgen.py

#!/usr/bin/env python3

# From https://github.com/difference-engine/thumbnail-generator-ubuntu (MIT License)
# Since the script is small and the maintainers seem inactive to accept my PR (#11) I decided to just copy it over.
# When it gets merged and the python package gets updated we can just use it

import os
import sys
from multiprocessing import Pool
from pathlib import Path
from typing import List, Union

import click
import gi
from loguru import logger
from tqdm import tqdm

gi.require_version("GnomeDesktop", "4.0")
from gi.repository import Gio, GnomeDesktop  # isort:skip

thumbnail_size_map = {
    "normal": GnomeDesktop.DesktopThumbnailSize.NORMAL,
    "large": GnomeDesktop.DesktopThumbnailSize.LARGE,
    "x-large": GnomeDesktop.DesktopThumbnailSize.XLARGE,
    "xx-large": GnomeDesktop.DesktopThumbnailSize.XXLARGE,
}

factory = None
logger.remove()
logger.add(sys.stdout, level="INFO")
logger.add("/tmp/thumbgen.log", level="DEBUG", rotation="100 MB")

def make_thumbnail(fpath: str) -> bool:
    mtime = os.path.getmtime(fpath)
    # Use Gio to determine the URI and mime type
    f = Gio.file_new_for_path(str(fpath))
    uri = f.get_uri()
    info = f.query_info("standard::content-type", Gio.FileQueryInfoFlags.NONE, None)
    mime_type = info.get_content_type()

    if factory.lookup(uri, mtime) is not None:
        logger.debug("FRESH       {}".format(uri))
        return False

    if not factory.can_thumbnail(uri, mime_type, mtime):
        logger.debug("UNSUPPORTED {}".format(uri))
        return False

    thumbnail = factory.generate_thumbnail(uri, mime_type)
    if thumbnail is None:
        logger.debug("ERROR       {}".format(uri))
        return False

    logger.debug("OK          {}".format(uri))
    factory.save_thumbnail(thumbnail, uri, mtime)
    return True


@logger.catch()
def thumbnail_folder(*, dir_path: Path, workers: int, only_images: bool, recursive: bool, machine_progress: bool = False) -> None:
    all_files = get_all_files(dir_path=dir_path, recursive=recursive)
    if only_images:
        all_files = get_all_images(all_files=all_files)
    all_files = [str(fpath) for fpath in all_files]
    if machine_progress:
        completed = 0
        total = len(all_files)
        with Pool(processes=workers) as p:
            for result in p.imap(make_thumbnail, all_files):
                completed += 1
                print(f"PROGRESS {completed}/{total} FILE {all_files[completed-1]}")
                sys.stdout.flush()
    else:
        with Pool(processes=workers) as p:
            list(tqdm(p.imap(make_thumbnail, all_files), total=len(all_files)))


def get_all_images(*, all_files: List[Path]) -> List[Path]:
    img_suffixes = [".jpg", ".jpeg", ".png", ".gif"]
    all_images = [fpath for fpath in all_files if fpath.suffix in img_suffixes]
    print("Found {} images".format(len(all_images)))
    return all_images


def get_all_files(*, dir_path: Path, recursive: bool) -> List[Path]:
    if not (dir_path.exists() and dir_path.is_dir()):
        raise ValueError("{} doesn't exist or isn't a valid directory!".format(dir_path.resolve()))
    if recursive:
        all_files = dir_path.rglob("*")
    else:
        all_files = dir_path.glob("*")
    all_files = [fpath for fpath in all_files if fpath.is_file()]
    print("Found {} files in the directory: {}".format(len(all_files), dir_path.resolve()))
    return all_files

@click.command()
@click.option(
    "-d", "--img_dirs", required=True, help='directories to generate thumbnails seperated by space, eg: "dir1/dir2 dir3"'
)
@click.option(
    "-s", "--size", default="normal", type=click.Choice(["normal", "large", "x-large", "xx-large"]), help="Thumbnail size: normal, large, x-large, xx-large"
)
@click.option("-w", "--workers", default=1, help="no of cpus to use for processing")
@click.option(
    "-i", "--only_images", is_flag=True, default=False, help="Whether to only look for images to be thumbnailed"
)
@click.option("-r", "--recursive", is_flag=True, default=False, help="Whether to recursively look for files")
@click.option("--machine_progress", is_flag=True, default=False, help="Print machine-readable progress lines instead of a progress bar")
def main(img_dirs: str, size: str, workers: str, only_images: bool, recursive: bool, machine_progress: bool) -> None:
    img_dirs = [Path(img_dir) for img_dir in img_dirs.split()]
    global factory
    factory = GnomeDesktop.DesktopThumbnailFactory.new(thumbnail_size_map[size])
    for img_dir in img_dirs:
        thumbnail_folder(dir_path=img_dir, workers=workers, only_images=only_images, recursive=recursive, machine_progress=machine_progress)
    print("Thumbnail Generation Completed!")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env bash
CONFIG_FILE="$HOME/.config/illogical-impulse/config.json"
JSON_PATH=".screenRecord.savePath"
CUSTOM_PATH=$(jq -r "$JSON_PATH" "$CONFIG_FILE" 2>/dev/null)
RECORDING_DIR=""
if [[ -n "$CUSTOM_PATH" ]]; then
    RECORDING_DIR="$CUSTOM_PATH"
else
    RECORDING_DIR="$HOME/Videos"
fi

set_recording_state() {
    local state=$1
    local STATE_FILE="$HOME/.local/state/quickshell/states.json"
    local tmp=$(mktemp)
    jq ".record.enable = $state" "$STATE_FILE" > "$tmp" && mv "$tmp" "$STATE_FILE"
}

getdate() {
    date '+%Y-%m-%d_%H.%M.%S'
}
getaudiooutput() {
    pactl list sources | grep 'Name' | grep 'monitor' | cut -d ' ' -f2
}

detect_compositor() {
    local combined
    combined="$(echo "${XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP:-} ${XDG_SESSION_DESKTOP:-}" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"
    if [[ "$combined" == *"niri"* ]]; then
        echo "niri"
    elif [[ "$combined" == *"hyprland"* ]]; then
        echo "hyprland"
    else
        echo "unknown"
    fi
}

getactivemonitor() {
    if [[ "$(detect_compositor)" == "niri" ]]; then
        niri msg -j workspaces | jq -r '.[] | select(.is_focused == true) | .output'
    else
        hyprctl monitors -j | jq -r '.[] | select(.focused == true) | .name'
    fi
}

mkdir -p "$RECORDING_DIR"
cd "$RECORDING_DIR" || exit

ARGS=("$@")
MANUAL_REGION=""
SOUND_FLAG=0
FULLSCREEN_FLAG=0
for ((i=0;i<${#ARGS[@]};i++)); do
    if [[ "${ARGS[i]}" == "--region" ]]; then
        if (( i+1 < ${#ARGS[@]} )); then
            MANUAL_REGION="${ARGS[i+1]}"
        else
            notify-send "Recording cancelled" "No region specified for --region" -a 'Recorder' & disown
            exit 1
        fi
    elif [[ "${ARGS[i]}" == "--sound" ]]; then
        SOUND_FLAG=1
    elif [[ "${ARGS[i]}" == "--fullscreen" ]]; then
        FULLSCREEN_FLAG=1
    fi
done

if pgrep wf-recorder > /dev/null; then
    notify-send "Recording Stopped" "Stopped" -a 'Recorder' &
    pkill wf-recorder &
    set_recording_state false
else
    if [[ $FULLSCREEN_FLAG -eq 1 ]]; then
        notify-send "Starting recording" 'recording_'"$(getdate)"'.mp4' -a 'Recorder' & disown
        set_recording_state true
        if [[ $SOUND_FLAG -eq 1 ]]; then
            wf-recorder -o "$(getactivemonitor)" --pixel-format yuv420p -f './recording_'"$(getdate)"'.mp4' -t --audio="$(getaudiooutput)"
        else
            wf-recorder -o "$(getactivemonitor)" --pixel-format yuv420p -f './recording_'"$(getdate)"'.mp4' -t
        fi
    else
        if [[ -n "$MANUAL_REGION" ]]; then
            region="$MANUAL_REGION"
        else
            if ! region="$(slurp 2>&1)"; then
                notify-send "Recording cancelled" "Selection was cancelled" -a 'Recorder' & disown
                exit 1
            fi
        fi
        notify-send "Starting recording" 'recording_'"$(getdate)"'.mp4' -a 'Recorder' & disown
        set_recording_state true
        if [[ $SOUND_FLAG -eq 1 ]]; then
            wf-recorder --pixel-format yuv420p -f './recording_'"$(getdate)"'.mp4' -t --geometry "$region" --audio="$(getaudiooutput)"
        else
            wf-recorder --pixel-format yuv420p -f './recording_'"$(getdate)"'.mp4' -t --geometry "$region"
        fi
    fi
    set_recording_state false
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# presets.sh - manage shell config presets | just for fun I could have done it from quickshell directly =P
# Usage:
#   presets.sh --save <name>
#   presets.sh --remove <name>
#   presets.sh --apply <name>

CONFIG_DIR="$HOME/.config/uchiha/quickshell"
CONFIG_FILE="$CONFIG_DIR/config.json"
PRESETS_DIR="$CONFIG_DIR/presets"
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
SWITCHWALL="$SCRIPT_DIR/colors/switchwall.sh"

mkdir -p "$PRESETS_DIR"

action="$1"
name="$2"

if [ -z "$name" ]; then
    echo "Error: missing preset name" >&2
    exit 1
fi

case "$action" in
    --save)
        description="$3"
        jq 'del(._presetMeta)' "$CONFIG_FILE" > "$PRESETS_DIR/${name}.json"
        if [ -n "$description" ]; then
            jq --arg desc "$description" '._presetMeta = {"description": $desc}' \
                "$PRESETS_DIR/${name}.json" > "$PRESETS_DIR/${name}.json.tmp" \
                && mv "$PRESETS_DIR/${name}.json.tmp" "$PRESETS_DIR/${name}.json"
        fi
        ;;
    --remove)
        rm -f "$PRESETS_DIR/${name}.json"
        ;;
    --apply)
        preset_file="$PRESETS_DIR/${name}.json"
        if [ ! -f "$preset_file" ]; then
            echo "Error: preset not found: $name" >&2
            exit 1
        fi
        jq -s '.[0] * .[1] | del(._presetMeta)' "$CONFIG_FILE" "$preset_file" \
            > "${CONFIG_FILE}.tmp" && mv "${CONFIG_FILE}.tmp" "$CONFIG_FILE"
        "$SWITCHWALL" --noswitch
        ;;
    *)
        echo "Error: unknown action: $action" >&2
        exit 1
        ;;
esac

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import calendar
import sys
import json
import google.auth.transport.requests
import google.oauth2.service_account

def get_token(json_str):
    try:
        # Load the string into a dictionary
        info = json.loads(json_str)
        
        # Initialize credentials
        creds = google.oauth2.service_account.Credentials.from_service_account_info(info)
        scoped_creds = creds.with_scopes(['https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform'])
        
        # Refresh to get the access token
        request = google.auth.transport.requests.Request()
        scoped_creds.refresh(request)

        token = scoped_creds.token
        expiry = int(calendar.timegm(scoped_creds.expiry.utctimetuple()))
        
        print(json.dumps({
            "token": token,
            "expiry": expiry
        }))

    except Exception as e:
        sys.stderr.write(f"Error: {str(e)}\n")
        sys.exit(1)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        sys.stderr.write("Usage: python3 get_token.py '<json_string>'\n")
        sys.exit(1)
    
    get_token(sys.argv[1])

pragma Singleton
pragma ComponentBehavior: Bound

import qs.modules.common.functions
import qs.modules.common
import QtQuick
import Quickshell

/**
 * Renders LaTeX snippets with MicroTeX.
 * For every request:
 *   1. Hash it
 *   2. Check if the hash is already processed
 *   3. If not, render it with MicroTeX and mark as processed
 */
Singleton {
    id: root
    
    readonly property var renderPadding: 4 // This is to prevent cutoff in the rendered images

    property list<string> processedHashes: []
    property var processedExpressions: ({})
    property var renderedImagePaths: ({})
    property string microtexBinaryDir: "/opt/MicroTeX"
    property string microtexBinaryName: "LaTeX"
    property string latexOutputPath: Directories.latexOutput

    signal renderFinished(string hash, string imagePath)

    /**
    * Requests rendering of a LaTeX expression.
    * Returns the [hash, isNew]
    */
    function requestRender(expression) {
        // 1. Hash it and initialize necessary variables
        const hash = Qt.md5(expression)
        const imagePath = `${latexOutputPath}/${hash}.svg`
        
        // 2. Check if the hash is already processed
        if (processedHashes.includes(hash)) {
            // console.log("Already processed: " + hash)
            renderFinished(hash, imagePath)
            return [hash, false]
        } else {
            root.processedHashes.push(hash)
            root.processedExpressions[hash] = expression
            // console.log("Rendering expression: " + expression)
        }

        // 3. If not, render it with MicroTeX and mark as processed
        // console.log(`[LatexRenderer] Rendering expression: ${expression} with hash: ${hash}`)
        // console.log(`                to file: ${imagePath}`)
        // console.log(`                with command: cd ${microtexBinaryDir} && ./${microtexBinaryName} -headless -input=${StringUtils.shellSingleQuoteEscape(expression)} -output=${imagePath} -textsize=${Appearance.font.pixelSize.normal} -padding=${renderPadding} -background=${Appearance.m3colors.m3tertiary} -foreground=${Appearance.m3colors.m3onTertiary} -maxwidth=0.85`)
        const processQml = `
            import Quickshell.Io
            Process {
                id: microtexProcess${hash}
                running: true
                command: [ "bash", "-c", 
                    "cd ${root.microtexBinaryDir} && ./${root.microtexBinaryName} -headless '-input=${StringUtils.shellSingleQuoteEscape(StringUtils.escapeBackslashes(expression))}' "
                    + "'-output=${imagePath}' " 
                    + "'-textsize=${Appearance.font.pixelSize.normal}' "
                    + "'-padding=${renderPadding}' "
                    // + "'-background=${Appearance.m3colors.m3tertiary}' "
                    + "'-foreground=${Appearance.colors.colOnLayer1}' "
                    + "-maxwidth=0.85 "
                ]
                // stdout: SplitParser {
                //     onRead: data => { console.log("MicroTeX: " + data) }
                // }
                onExited: (exitCode, exitStatus) => {
                    // console.log("[LatexRenderer] MicroTeX process exited with code: " + exitCode + ", status: " + exitStatus)
                    renderedImagePaths["${hash}"] = "${imagePath}"
                    root.renderFinished("${hash}", "${imagePath}")
                    microtexProcess${hash}.destroy()
                }
            }
        `
        // console.log("MicroTeX: " + processQml)
        Qt.createQmlObject(processQml, root, `MicroTeXProcess_${hash}`)
        return [hash, true]
    }
}


==================================================
FILE: ./services/ResourceUsage.qml
==================================================

pragma Singleton
pragma ComponentBehavior: Bound

import qs.modules.common
import QtQuick
import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Io

/**
 * Simple polled resource usage service with RAM, Swap, CPU and Disk usage.
 */
Singleton {
    id: root
    property real memoryTotal: 1
    property real memoryFree: 0
    property real memoryUsed: memoryTotal - memoryFree
    property real memoryUsedPercentage: memoryUsed / memoryTotal
    property real swapTotal: 1
    property real swapFree: 0
    property real swapUsed: swapTotal - swapFree
    property real swapUsedPercentage: swapTotal > 0 ? (swapUsed / swapTotal) : 0
    property real cpuUsage: 0
    property var previousCpuStats

    property string maxAvailableMemoryString: kbToGbString(ResourceUsage.memoryTotal)
    property string maxAvailableSwapString: kbToGbString(ResourceUsage.swapTotal)
    property string maxAvailableCpuString: "--"

    readonly property int historyLength: Config?.options.resources.historyLength ?? 60
    property list<real> cpuUsageHistory: []
    property list<real> memoryUsageHistory: []
    property list<real> swapUsageHistory: []

    property real cpuTemp: 0

    property real diskTotal: 1
    property real diskUsed: 0
    property real diskFree: 0
    property real diskUsedPercentage: diskTotal > 0 ? diskUsed / diskTotal : 0
    property list<real> diskUsageHistory: []
    property string maxAvailableDiskString: kbToGbString(diskTotal)

    Process {
        id: tempProc
        command: ["bash", "-c", "sensors 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'Package id 0|Tctl|Tdie' | grep -oP '\\+\\K[0-9.]+(?=°C)' | head -1"]
        stdout: StdioCollector {
            onStreamFinished: {
                root.cpuTemp = parseFloat(text.trim())
            }
        }
    }

    Process {
        id: diskProc
        command: ["bash", "-c", "df -k / | awk 'NR==2{print $2,$3,$4}'"]
        stdout: StdioCollector {
            onStreamFinished: {
                const parts = text.trim().split(" ").map(Number)
                if (parts.length >= 3) {
                    root.diskTotal = parts[0]
                    root.diskUsed  = parts[1]
                    root.diskFree  = parts[2]
                }
            }
        }
    }

    Timer {
        interval: Config?.options.resources.updateInterval ?? 3000
        running: true
        repeat: true
        onTriggered: {
            tempProc.running = false
            tempProc.running = true
            diskProc.running = false
            diskProc.running = true
        }
    }

    function kbToGbString(kb) {
        return (kb / (1024 * 1024)).toFixed(1) + " GB"
    }

    function updateMemoryUsageHistory() {
        memoryUsageHistory = [...memoryUsageHistory, memoryUsedPercentage]
        if (memoryUsageHistory.length > historyLength) memoryUsageHistory.shift()
    }
    function updateSwapUsageHistory() {
        swapUsageHistory = [...swapUsageHistory, swapUsedPercentage]
        if (swapUsageHistory.length > historyLength) swapUsageHistory.shift()
    }
    function updateCpuUsageHistory() {
        cpuUsageHistory = [...cpuUsageHistory, cpuUsage]
        if (cpuUsageHistory.length > historyLength) cpuUsageHistory.shift()
    }
    function updateDiskUsageHistory() {
        diskUsageHistory = [...diskUsageHistory, diskUsedPercentage]
        if (diskUsageHistory.length > historyLength) diskUsageHistory.shift()
    }
    function updateHistories() {
        updateMemoryUsageHistory()
        updateSwapUsageHistory()
        updateCpuUsageHistory()
        updateDiskUsageHistory()
    }

    Timer {
        interval: 1
        running: true
        repeat: true
        onTriggered: {
            fileMeminfo.reload()
            fileStat.reload()

            const textMeminfo = fileMeminfo.text()
            memoryTotal = Number(textMeminfo.match(/MemTotal: *(\d+)/)?.[1] ?? 1)
            memoryFree  = Number(textMeminfo.match(/MemAvailable: *(\d+)/)?.[1] ?? 0)
            swapTotal   = Number(textMeminfo.match(/SwapTotal: *(\d+)/)?.[1] ?? 1)
            swapFree    = Number(textMeminfo.match(/SwapFree: *(\d+)/)?.[1] ?? 0)

            const textStat = fileStat.text()
            const cpuLine  = textStat.match(/^cpu\s+(\d+)\s+(\d+)\s+(\d+)\s+(\d+)\s+(\d+)\s+(\d+)\s+(\d+)/)
            if (cpuLine) {
                const stats = cpuLine.slice(1).map(Number)
                const total = stats.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0)
                const idle  = stats[3]
                if (previousCpuStats) {
                    const totalDiff = total - previousCpuStats.total
                    const idleDiff  = idle  - previousCpuStats.idle
                    cpuUsage = totalDiff > 0 ? (1 - idleDiff / totalDiff) : 0
                }
                previousCpuStats = { total, idle }
            }

            root.updateHistories()
            interval = Config.options?.resources?.updateInterval ?? 3000
        }
    }

    FileView { id: fileMeminfo; path: "/proc/meminfo" }
    FileView { id: fileStat;    path: "/proc/stat" }

    Process {
        id: findCpuMaxFreqProc
        environment: ({ LANG: "C", LC_ALL: "C" })
        command: ["bash", "-c", "lscpu | grep 'CPU max MHz' | awk '{print $4}'"]
        running: true
        stdout: StdioCollector {
            id: outputCollector
            onStreamFinished: {
                root.maxAvailableCpuString = (parseFloat(outputCollector.text) / 1000).toFixed(0) + " GHz"
            }
        }
    }
}

==================================================
FILE: ./services/SongRec.qml
==================================================

pragma Singleton
pragma ComponentBehavior: Bound

import qs.modules.common
import QtQuick
import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Io

Singleton {
    id: root

    enum MonitorSource { Monitor, Input }

    property var monitorSource: SongRec.MonitorSource.Monitor
    property int timeoutInterval: Config.options.musicRecognition.interval
    property int timeoutDuration: Config.options.musicRecognition.timeout
    readonly property bool running: recognizeMusicProc.running

    function toggleRunning(running) {
        if (recognizeMusicProc.running && !running === true) root.manuallyStopped = true;
        if (running != undefined) {
            recognizeMusicProc.running = running
        } else {
            recognizeMusicProc.running = !root.running
        }
        musicReconizedProc.running = false
    }

    function toggleMonitorSource(source) {
        if (source !== undefined) {
            root.monitorSource = source
            return
        }
        root.monitorSource = (root.monitorSource === SongRec.MonitorSource.Monitor) ? SongRec.MonitorSource.Input : SongRec.MonitorSource.Monitor
    }
    function monitorSourceToString(source) {
        if (source === SongRec.MonitorSource.Monitor) {
            return "monitor"
        } else {
            return "input"
        }
    }
    readonly property string monitorSourceString: monitorSourceToString(monitorSource)
    property var recognizedTrack: ({ title:"", subtitle:"", url:""})
    property bool manuallyStopped: false

    function handleRecognition(jsonText) {
        try {
            var obj = JSON.parse(jsonText)
            root.recognizedTrack = {
                title: obj.track.title,
                subtitle: obj.track.subtitle,
                url: obj.track.url
            }
            musicReconizedProc.running = true
        } catch(e) {
            Quickshell.execDetached(["notify-send", Translation.tr("Couldn't recognize music"), Translation.tr("Perhaps what you're listening to is too niche"), "-a", "Shell"])
        }
    }

    Process {
        id: recognizeMusicProc
        running: false
        command: [`${Directories.scriptPath}/musicRecognition/recognize-music.sh`, "-i", root.timeoutInterval, "-t", root.timeoutDuration, "-s", root.monitorSourceString]
        stdout: StdioCollector {
            onStreamFinished: {
                if (root.manuallyStopped) {
                    root.manuallyStopped = false
                    return
                }
                handleRecognition(this.text)
            }
        }
        onExited: (exitCode, exitStatus) => {
            if (exitCode === 1) {
                Quickshell.execDetached(["notify-send", Translation.tr("Couldn't recognize music"), Translation.tr("Make sure you have songrec installed"), "-a", "Shell"])
            }
        }
    }

    Process {
        id: musicReconizedProc
        running: false
        command: [
            "notify-send",
            Translation.tr("Music Recognized"), 
            root.recognizedTrack.title + " - " + root.recognizedTrack.subtitle, 
            "-A", "Shazam",
            "-A", "YouTube",
            "-a", "Shell"
        ]
        stdout: StdioCollector {
            onStreamFinished: {
                if (this.text === "") return
                if (this.text == 0) {
                    Qt.openUrlExternally(root.recognizedTrack.url);
                } else {
                    Qt.openUrlExternally("https://www.youtube.com/results?search_query=" + root.recognizedTrack.title + " - " + root.recognizedTrack.subtitle);
                }
            }
        }
    }
}


==================================================
FILE: ./services/StudyLog.qml
==================================================

pragma Singleton
pragma ComponentBehavior: Bound

import qs.services
import qs.modules.common
import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Io
import QtQuick

/**
 * Append-only log of completed study blocks — one JSON object per line
 * (JSON Lines) in `studylog.jsonl`, so it stays easy to tail/grep or parse
 * from an external script too, and never needs a full rewrite-the-whole-
 * file save. This file is the single source of truth for "has this
 * specific occurrence of this block already been completed" — that's
 * what makes it safe to restart the shell without re-logging or
 * re-notifying for sessions that already finished.
 *
 * Each line looks like:
 *   {"id":"m4x2f9a1b","date":"2026-08-07","day":4,"label":"Physics",
 *    "startMinute":540,"endMinute":600,"scheduledStart":"9:00 AM",
 *    "scheduledEnd":"10:00 AM","minutes":60,"longSession":false,
 *    "noBreak":false,"status":"completed","completedAt":1754562000}
 *
 * `minutes` is the block's full scheduled duration — this counts break
 * time as part of a dedicated study block rather than trying to track
 * focus-only seconds, which keeps the log meaningful even if you
 * paused/resumed mid-block.
 *
 * A second, derived file — `studydaily.jsonl` — is rewritten (not
 * appended) every time a new session lands, and holds one clean,
 * human-friendly rollup line per calendar date: total minutes studied
 * that day, session count, and the list of blocks. That's the file to
 * read if you just want "how much did I study today / this week", the
 * per-session file above is the append-only raw record.
 */
Singleton {
    id: root
    property string filePath: Directories.studyLogPath
    property string dailyFilePath: Directories.studyDailyPath
    property var entries: []
    // Guards StudyScheduler against acting before the log has loaded at
    // least once after a shell (re)start — without this, the very first
    // poll after launch could run before `entries` reflects what's
    // already on disk and re-log/re-notify something that finished
    // before this launch.
    property bool loaded: false

    function _dateKey(d) {
        d = d || new Date()
        const mm = (d.getMonth() + 1).toString().padStart(2, "0")
        const dd = d.getDate().toString().padStart(2, "0")
        return d.getFullYear() + "-" + mm + "-" + dd
    }

    function todayKey() {
        return root._dateKey(new Date())
    }

    // Has this exact occurrence (schedule entry id, on this date) already
    // been logged as completed? This is the persisted check StudyScheduler
    // uses instead of its in-memory-only dedupe, so a shell relaunch after
    // a block already ended does NOT re-log or re-notify it.
    function hasCompleted(id, dateKey) {
        return root.entries.some(e => e.id === id && e.date === dateKey)
    }

    function record(entry, minutesStudied, dateKey, status) {
        dateKey = dateKey || root.todayKey()
        const line = JSON.stringify({
            "id": entry.id,
            "date": dateKey,
            "day": entry.day,
            "label": entry.label,
            "startMinute": entry.startMinute,
            "endMinute": entry.endMinute,
            "scheduledStart": StudySchedule.formatMinute(entry.startMinute),
            "scheduledEnd": StudySchedule.formatMinute(entry.endMinute),
            "minutes": minutesStudied,
            "longSession": !!entry.longSession,
            "noBreak": !!entry.noBreak,
            "status": status || "completed",
            "completedAt": Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000)
        })
        const dir = root.filePath.substring(0, root.filePath.lastIndexOf("/"))
        const escaped = line.replace(/'/g, "'\\''")
        appendProc.command = ["bash", "-c",
            "mkdir -p '" + dir + "' && printf '%s\\n' '" + escaped + "' >> '" + root.filePath + "'"
        ]
        appendProc.running = true
    }

    // Total minutes studied on a given Date (defaults to today).
    function minutesOn(d) {
        const key = root._dateKey(d)
        return root.entries.filter(e => e.date === key).reduce((sum, e) => sum + e.minutes, 0)
    }

    function minutesToday() {
        return root.minutesOn(new Date())
    }

    function formatDuration(mins) {
        const h = Math.floor(mins / 60)
        const m = Math.round(mins % 60)
        if (h > 0) return h + "h " + m + "m"
        return m + "m"
    }

    // Rebuilds the organized daily rollup from `entries` and writes it
    // out. Cheap (this log is a handful of entries a day) and simplest
    // to just regenerate in full rather than patch in place.
    function _rebuildDailyRollup() {
        const byDate = {}
        for (const e of root.entries) {
            if (!byDate[e.date]) {
                byDate[e.date] = { "totalMinutes": 0, "totalFormatted": "", "sessions": 0, "blocks": [] }
            }
            byDate[e.date].totalMinutes += e.minutes
            byDate[e.date].sessions += 1
            byDate[e.date].blocks.push({
                "label": e.label,
                "start": e.scheduledStart ?? StudySchedule.formatMinute(e.startMinute),
                "end": e.scheduledEnd ?? StudySchedule.formatMinute(e.endMinute),
                "minutes": e.minutes,
                "status": e.status ?? "completed"
            })
        }
        for (const key of Object.keys(byDate)) {
            byDate[key].totalFormatted = root.formatDuration(byDate[key].totalMinutes)
        }
        dailyRollupView.setText(JSON.stringify(byDate, null, 2))
    }

    function refresh() {
        logFileView.reload()
    }

    Component.onCompleted: refresh()

    Process {
        id: appendProc
        running: false
        stderr: SplitParser {
            splitMarker: "\n"
            onRead: function(line) {
                if (line.trim() !== "")
                    console.warn("[StudyLog] failed to append:", line)
            }
        }
        // The append happens out-of-band via bash, so pull the file back
        // in once it's done to keep `entries` (and minutesToday(),
        // hasCompleted()) fresh, and regenerate the daily rollup.
        onExited: root.refresh()
    }

    FileView {
        id: logFileView
        path: Qt.resolvedUrl(root.filePath)
        watchChanges: true
        onFileChanged: logFileView.reload()
        onLoaded: {
            const text = logFileView.text()
            const lines = text.split("\n").filter(l => l.trim().length > 0)
            const parsed = []
            for (const l of lines) {
                try { parsed.push(JSON.parse(l)) } catch (e) { /* skip bad line */ }
            }
            root.entries = parsed
            root.loaded = true
            root._rebuildDailyRollup()
        }
        onLoadFailed: (error) => {
            if (error == FileViewError.FileNotFound) {
                root.entries = []
                root.loaded = true
            } else {
                console.log("[StudyLog] Error loading file: " + error)
            }
        }
    }

    // Write-only view for the derived daily rollup — source of truth is
    // always `entries` (from logFileView above), this is regenerated
    // wholesale on every change rather than read back in.
    FileView {
        id: dailyRollupView
        path: Qt.resolvedUrl(root.dailyFilePath)
    }
}



==================================================
FILE: ./services/StudySchedule.qml
==================================================

pragma Singleton
pragma ComponentBehavior: Bound

import qs.modules.common
import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Io
import QtQuick

/**
 * Weekly study/time-table schedule — hybrid model.
 *
 * `list` holds recurring TEMPLATES, one per weekday pattern:
 *   {
 *     id:            string, generated
 *     day:           int, 0 = Sunday .. 6 = Saturday (matches JS Date.getDay())
 *     label:         string
 *     startMinute:   int, minutes since midnight (0-1439)
 *     endMinute:     int, minutes since midnight, must be > startMinute
 *     enabled:       bool
 *     longSession:   bool, 45 min focus / 5 min break instead of 25 / 5
 *                    (ignored when noBreak is true)
 *     noBreak:       bool, one continuous focus lap for the whole block,
 *                    no break cycling — duration can be any length
 *   }
 * A template recurs on that weekday every week, forever, until deleted.
 *
 * `overrides` holds per-date EXCEPTIONS, each tied to a specific calendar
 * date ("YYYY-MM-DD"), so editing/skipping one occurrence never touches
 * other weeks:
 *   {
 *     id:          string, generated ("ov-" prefixed)
 *     templateId:  string | null   — null means this override is a
 *                  standalone one-off block that exists only on `date`
 *                  and isn't tied to any recurring template
 *     date:        "YYYY-MM-DD"
 *     type:        "modify" | "skip" | "add"
 *       "modify" — replaces a template occurrence's fields on this date
 *                  only (label/startMinute/endMinute/longSession/
 *                  noBreak/enabled all present)
 *       "skip"   — removes a template occurrence on this date only
 *       "add"    — a standalone one-off block on this date (templateId
 *                  is null; label/startMinute/... all present)
 *   }
 *
 * effectiveEntriesForDate(date) merges templates + that date's overrides
 * into what should actually happen on that specific calendar day — that's
 * what StudyScheduler, and the widget's day view, should always read from.
 *
 * Persisted as plain JSON: { "templates": [...], "overrides": [...] }.
 * (Older files that were just a bare array of templates still load fine —
 * they're treated as templates with no overrides.)
 */
Singleton {
    id: root
    property var filePath: Directories.studySchedulePath
    property var list: []       // recurring templates
    property var overrides: []  // per-date exceptions

    // Display order is Monday-first (Mon→Sun). Note this is purely a
    // display-order array: the `day` field on templates/overrides still
    // follows JS Date.getDay() (0 = Sunday .. 6 = Saturday) everywhere
    // else in this file — anything indexing into these two arrays with a
    // raw .getDay() value needs (.getDay() + 6) % 7 instead.
    readonly property var dayNames: ["Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday", "Thursday", "Friday", "Saturday", "Sunday"]
    readonly property var dayShort: ["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun"]

    readonly property int minFocusMinutes: 25
    readonly property int breakMinutes: 5
    readonly property int longFocusMinutes: 45

    // Any positive duration is valid now — no more forced 25-min minimum
    // or multiple-of-5 requirement. What actually happens at runtime:
    //  - duration <= the cadence unit (25 min, or 45 with longSession):
    //    runs as one continuous focus lap for the whole block, same as
    //    an explicit "No break" block — there's no point starting the
    //    break-cycling machinery for something that'll never reach a
    //    break before the block ends anyway.
    //  - duration > the unit: cycles focus(unit)/break(5)/focus(unit)/...
    //    same as before, but the block's own end time is always what
    //    cuts the LAST leg short rather than requiring the total to
    //    divide evenly — e.g. a 47-min block runs 25 focus, 5 break,
    //    then a 17-min focus leg that just ends when the block does.
    //  - noBreak blocks: same as always, one continuous lap for the
    //    exact block length, any duration.
    // See expectedNoBreakFor()/focusMinutesFor() below — StudyScheduler
    // uses those, not this duration, to decide how to actually drive it.
    function isValidDuration(startMinute, endMinute, noBreak) {
        // Equal start/end is the only real invalid case (zero length).
        // endMinute < startMinute is NOT invalid — it means the block
        // runs past midnight into the next day. Storage always keeps
        // endMinute > startMinute by adding 1440 for a crossing block
        // (see SidebarStudySchedule.save()); this just validates the
        // clock values the person actually typed, before that shift.
        return endMinute !== startMinute
    }

    // Whether this entry should run as one continuous focus lap at
    // runtime — either because "No break" was explicitly toggled, or
    // because the block's own duration is short enough that a single
    // cadence unit (25/45 min) would never even reach a break before the
    // block ends anyway.
    function expectedNoBreakFor(entry) {
        if (entry.noBreak) return true
            const unit = entry.longSession ? root.longFocusMinutes : root.minFocusMinutes
            const duration = entry.endMinute - entry.startMinute
            return duration <= unit
    }

    function focusMinutesFor(entry) {
        if (root.expectedNoBreakFor(entry)) return entry.endMinute - entry.startMinute
            return entry.longSession ? root.longFocusMinutes : root.minFocusMinutes
    }

    function dateKeyFor(d) {
        if (!d) d = new Date()
            const mm = (d.getMonth() + 1).toString().padStart(2, "0")
            const dd = d.getDate().toString().padStart(2, "0")
            return d.getFullYear() + "-" + mm + "-" + dd
    }

    function _save() {
        // Reassign to trigger change notification for anything bound to
        // root.list / root.overrides.
        root.list = list.slice(0)
        root.overrides = overrides.slice(0)
        scheduleFileView.setText(JSON.stringify({ "templates": root.list, "overrides": root.overrides }))
    }

    function _genId() {
        return Date.now().toString(36) + Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 7)
    }

    function _genOverrideId() {
        return "ov-" + Date.now().toString(36) + Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 7)
    }

    // ── Templates (recurring, every week) ──────────────────────────────
    function addEntry(day, label, startMinute, endMinute, longSession, noBreak) {
        list.push({
            "id": root._genId(),
                  "day": day,
                  "label": label,
                  "startMinute": startMinute,
                  "endMinute": endMinute,
                  "enabled": true,
                  "longSession": !!longSession,
                  "noBreak": !!noBreak
        })
        root._save()
    }

    // Edits the template itself — affects every week, past overrides for
    // other dates are untouched.
    function updateEntry(id, patch) {
        const idx = list.findIndex(e => e.id === id)
        if (idx === -1) return
            list[idx] = Object.assign({}, list[idx], patch)
            root._save()
    }

    function toggleEnabled(id) {
        const idx = list.findIndex(e => e.id === id)
        if (idx === -1) return
            list[idx].enabled = !list[idx].enabled
            root._save()
    }

    // Like toggleEnabled(), but for an entry object returned from
    // effectiveEntriesForDate() rather than a raw template id. A plain
    // recurring entry toggles the template (every week); a standalone
    // one-off or a "just this date" modification toggles that override
    // instead, so it doesn't silently no-op trying to find a template
    // that doesn't exist (standalone) or affect every other week when
    // you only meant to disable one date (modified).
    function toggleEnabledForEffectiveEntry(entry) {
        if (entry.isOverride) {
            root.updateOverride(entry.overrideId, { "enabled": !entry.enabled })
        } else {
            root.toggleEnabled(entry.id)
        }
    }

    // Deletes a recurring template entirely (every week, going forward)
    // and cleans up any per-date overrides that referenced it.
    function deleteTemplate(id) {
        const idx = list.findIndex(e => e.id === id)
        if (idx !== -1) list.splice(idx, 1)
            root.overrides = root.overrides.filter(o => o.templateId !== id)
            root._save()
    }

    function entriesForDay(day) {
        return list.filter(e => e.day === day).sort((a, b) => a.startMinute - b.startMinute)
    }

    // ── Per-date overrides ───────────────────────────────────────────────
    // Modify a single occurrence of a recurring template, only for one date.
    function overrideModify(templateId, date, patch) {
        const dateKey = root.dateKeyFor(date)
        root.overrides = root.overrides.filter(o => !(o.templateId === templateId && o.date === dateKey))
        root.overrides.push(Object.assign({
            "id": root._genOverrideId(),
                                          "templateId": templateId,
                                          "date": dateKey,
                                          "type": "modify"
        }, patch))
        root._save()
    }

    // Skip a single occurrence of a recurring template for one date —
    // supersedes any existing modify override for that template+date.
    function overrideSkip(templateId, date) {
        const dateKey = root.dateKeyFor(date)
        root.overrides = root.overrides.filter(o => !(o.templateId === templateId && o.date === dateKey))
        root.overrides.push({
            "id": root._genOverrideId(),
                            "templateId": templateId,
                            "date": dateKey,
                            "type": "skip"
        })
        root._save()
    }

    // A one-off block that exists only on this date, not tied to any
    // recurring template.
    function addOneOff(date, label, startMinute, endMinute, longSession, noBreak) {
        const dateKey = root.dateKeyFor(date)
        root.overrides.push({
            "id": root._genOverrideId(),
                            "templateId": null,
                            "date": dateKey,
                            "type": "add",
                            "label": label,
                            "startMinute": startMinute,
                            "endMinute": endMinute,
                            "enabled": true,
                            "longSession": !!longSession,
                            "noBreak": !!noBreak
        })
        root._save()
    }

    // Edits an existing override in place — used for a standalone one-off,
    // or to re-edit a "just this date" modification.
    function updateOverride(overrideId, patch) {
        const idx = overrides.findIndex(o => o.id === overrideId)
        if (idx === -1) return
            overrides[idx] = Object.assign({}, overrides[idx], patch)
            root._save()
    }

    // Removes an override: a "modify" reverts that date back to the plain
    // template; an "add" just deletes the one-off block. ("skip" overrides
    // are normally replaced via overrideSkip/overrideModify rather than
    // removed, but this works for that too if ever needed.)
    function removeOverride(overrideId) {
        root.overrides = root.overrides.filter(o => o.id !== overrideId)
        root._save()
    }

    // What should actually happen on this specific calendar date: that
    // weekday's templates, with the date's overrides applied (modified /
    // skipped / added). This is what StudyScheduler and the widget's day
    // view should always read from — never entriesForDay() directly, or
    // per-date overrides get silently ignored.
    function effectiveEntriesForDate(date) {
        if (!date) date = new Date()
            const dateKey = root.dateKeyFor(date)
            const weekday = date.getDay()
            const templates = root.entriesForDay(weekday)
            const overridesForDate = root.overrides.filter(o => o.date === dateKey)

            const skipSet = {}
            overridesForDate.filter(o => o.type === "skip").forEach(o => { skipSet[o.templateId] = true })
            const modifyMap = {}
            overridesForDate.filter(o => o.type === "modify").forEach(o => { modifyMap[o.templateId] = o })

            const result = []
            for (const t of templates) {
                if (skipSet[t.id]) continue
                    const o = modifyMap[t.id]
                    if (o) {
                        result.push(Object.assign({}, t, {
                            "label": o.label, "startMinute": o.startMinute, "endMinute": o.endMinute,
                            "longSession": o.longSession, "noBreak": o.noBreak, "enabled": o.enabled,
                            "isOverride": true, "overrideId": o.id, "templateId": t.id, "standalone": false
                        }))
                    } else {
                        result.push(Object.assign({}, t, { "isOverride": false, "templateId": t.id, "standalone": false }))
                    }
            }
            overridesForDate.filter(o => o.type === "add").forEach(o => {
                result.push({
                    "id": o.id, "templateId": null, "day": weekday,
                    "label": o.label, "startMinute": o.startMinute, "endMinute": o.endMinute,
                    "enabled": o.enabled, "longSession": o.longSession, "noBreak": o.noBreak,
                    "isOverride": true, "overrideId": o.id, "standalone": true
                })
            })
            return result.sort((a, b) => a.startMinute - b.startMinute)
    }

    // Entries that started on the PREVIOUS calendar date and run past
    // midnight into `date` (stored endMinute >= 1440). Kept with their
    // ORIGINAL startMinute/endMinute (so formatMinute() keeps showing
    // their real clock time, e.g. "11:00 PM – 1:00 AM"), plus:
    //   ownerDateKey   — the date this block actually belongs to / is
    //                    logged under (yesterday, not today)
    //   relativeStart / relativeEnd — start/end shifted onto TODAY's
    //                    0-1439 clock (relativeStart negative), for
    //                    sorting and for comparing against "now"
    //   carriedFromPrevDay — true, so callers can label it distinctly
    //                    from a block that starts today and runs into
    //                    tomorrow
    function crossMidnightEntriesInto(date) {
        if (!date) date = new Date()
            const prevDate = new Date(date)
            prevDate.setDate(date.getDate() - 1)
            const ownerDateKey = root.dateKeyFor(prevDate)
            const prevEntries = root.effectiveEntriesForDate(prevDate)
            return prevEntries
            .filter(e => e.endMinute >= 1440)
            .map(e => Object.assign({}, e, {
                "ownerDateKey": ownerDateKey,
                "relativeStart": e.startMinute - 1440,
                "relativeEnd": e.endMinute - 1440,
                "carriedFromPrevDay": true
            }))
    }

    // Everything actually relevant to `date` for "what's happening right
    // now" / live-tracking purposes: that date's own entries, plus the
    // tail of anything carried over from the day before. This is what
    // StudyScheduler.check() and any "current/live" view should read —
    // effectiveEntriesForDate() alone doesn't know about the part of an
    // overnight block that lands on the following day.
    function activeEntriesForDate(date) {
        if (!date) date = new Date()
            const ownerDateKey = root.dateKeyFor(date)
            const own = root.effectiveEntriesForDate(date).map(e => Object.assign({}, e, {
                "ownerDateKey": ownerDateKey,
                "relativeStart": e.startMinute,
                "relativeEnd": e.endMinute,
                "carriedFromPrevDay": false
            }))
            return own.concat(root.crossMidnightEntriesInto(date))
            .sort((a, b) => a.relativeStart - b.relativeStart)
    }

    function minutesNow(d) {
        return d.getHours() * 60 + d.getMinutes()
    }

    // The block that's running right now, or null. Uses activeEntriesForDate
    // so a block that started yesterday and hasn't hit its end time yet
    // still shows as current after midnight.
    function currentEntry() {
        const now = new Date()
        const mins = root.minutesNow(now)
        const todays = root.activeEntriesForDate(now).filter(e => e.enabled)
        for (const e of todays) {
            if (mins >= e.relativeStart && mins < e.relativeEnd) return e
        }
        return null
    }

    // Up to `limit` upcoming blocks: rest of today first, then tomorrow.
    // Each returned entry is tagged with a `dayLabel` of "Today" or "Tomorrow".
    function upcomingEntries(limit) {
        limit = limit || 4
        const now = new Date()
        const mins = root.minutesNow(now)
        const result = []

        const todays = root.effectiveEntriesForDate(now).filter(e => e.enabled && e.startMinute > mins)
        for (const e of todays) {
            if (result.length >= limit) break
                result.push(Object.assign({}, e, { "dayLabel": "Today" }))
        }

        if (result.length < limit) {
            const tomorrow = new Date(now.getTime() + 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000)
            const tomorrows = root.effectiveEntriesForDate(tomorrow).filter(e => e.enabled)
            for (const e of tomorrows) {
                if (result.length >= limit) break
                    result.push(Object.assign({}, e, { "dayLabel": "Tomorrow" }))
            }
        }

        return result
    }

    // m can be >= 1440 for a block that crosses midnight (storage keeps
    // endMinute > startMinute by adding a full day rather than wrapping),
    // so normalize to a 0-23 hour before formatting.
    function formatMinute(m) {
        const h = Math.floor(m / 60) % 24
        const mm = m % 60
        const period = h < 12 ? "AM" : "PM"
        let h12 = h % 12
        if (h12 === 0) h12 = 12
            return h12 + ":" + (mm < 10 ? "0" + mm : mm) + " " + period
    }

    function refresh() {
        scheduleFileView.reload()
    }

    Component.onCompleted: refresh()

    FileView {
        id: scheduleFileView
        path: Qt.resolvedUrl(root.filePath)
        onLoaded: {
            try {
                const parsed = JSON.parse(scheduleFileView.text())
                if (Array.isArray(parsed)) {
                    // Old format: bare array of templates, no overrides yet.
                    root.list = parsed
                    root.overrides = []
                } else {
                    root.list = parsed.templates || []
                    root.overrides = parsed.overrides || []
                }
            } catch (e) {
                console.log("[StudySchedule] Failed to parse file, starting empty:", e)
                root.list = []
                root.overrides = []
            }
            console.log("[StudySchedule] File loaded")
        }
        onLoadFailed: (error) => {
            if (error == FileViewError.FileNotFound) {
                console.log("[StudySchedule] File not found, creating new file.")
                root.list = []
                root.overrides = []
                scheduleFileView.setText(JSON.stringify({ "templates": root.list, "overrides": root.overrides }))
            } else {
                console.log("[StudySchedule] Error loading file: " + error)
            }
        }
    }
}

FILE: ./services/StudyScheduler.qml

pragma Singleton
pragma ComponentBehavior: Bound

import qs.services
import qs.modules.common

import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Io
import QtQuick

// ── StudyScheduler ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Watches StudySchedule against real time, all the time (once instantiated —
// see the `load()` note below), regardless of whether any widget is open.
// It always reads StudySchedule.effectiveEntriesForDate(today) — the
// recurring weekly templates with that specific date's overrides
// (modified/skipped/one-off blocks) already applied — so edits made "just
// for this date" in the widget are respected without any extra handling
// here.
//
//   - notifyLeadMinutes before a block starts -> "starting soon" notification
//   - at block start                          -> starts TimerService's pomodoro
//                                                 using that block's own
//                                                 focus/break lengths (25/5,
//                                                 45/5 if longSession, or a
//                                                 single continuous lap if
//                                                 noBreak) via
//                                                 startScheduledSessionAt().
//                                                 If the block already
//                                                 started before this launch
//                                                 (e.g. shell comes up 7 min
//                                                 into a block), it resyncs
//                                                 to the correct phase and
//                                                 elapsed offset instead of
//                                                 restarting a fresh lap.
//   - at block end                            -> stops the pomodoro via
//                                                 endScheduledSession() and
//                                                 records the block in
//                                                 StudyLog for daily totals
//
// ── Reconciliation ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Every poll, `check()` works out `shouldBe`: the one enabled, in-window,
// not-yet-completed block that OUGHT to be driving the pomodoro right now
// (or null). It compares that against what's ACTUALLY driving it —
// Persistent.states.timer.pomodoro.scheduleEntryId/scheduleDateKey, which
// TimerService.startScheduledSessionAt() persists and survives a shell
// restart. Three cases fall out of that comparison:
//
//   1. Something's driving it but shouldn't be anymore -> stop it
//      (TimerService.endScheduledSession()). This is what fixes: toggling
//      a block off mid-session (it drops out of `shouldBe` immediately,
//      since disabled blocks are skipped), deleting/skipping it mid-
//      session, its window ending naturally, AND a stale session left
//      running from before a shell restart whose block no longer matches
//      (e.g. you disabled it, or the shell was closed for so long the
//      block's window has since passed). Logs the real elapsed time in
//      StudyLog either way, capped at the block's own scheduled length —
//      a manual disable/delete/edit mid-session still gets credited for
//      however long you actually studied, it's just tagged
//      "stopped-early" instead of "completed".
//   2. The right block is driving it, but its own settings changed
//      (time/cadence edited mid-session) -> resync: restart the pomodoro
//      with the new focus/break lengths, still anchored to the block's
//      real start time so elapsed time stays correct. This is what fixes
//      "editing mid-session doesn't take effect".
//   3. Nothing's driving it but something should be -> start it.
//
// Because all of this reads Persistent state rather than an in-memory
// cache, it's naturally restart-safe too: on the very first poll after a
// relaunch, whatever `scheduleEntryId` was left over from before the
// restart gets compared against `shouldBe` same as any other poll, and
// stopped/resynced/logged exactly as if the shell had never restarted at
// all — that's what fixes a toggled-off session still ticking away after
// a relaunch.
//
// IMPORTANT: like Wallpapers.qml / Updates.qml / LyricsService.qml in this
// project, this is a `pragma Singleton` and QML only instantiates singletons
// lazily, on first access. Call `StudyScheduler.load()` once from
// shell.qml's Component.onCompleted (next to the other `.load()` calls) so
// the poll timer below actually starts at shell startup instead of only
// when someone opens the schedule editor.
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Singleton {
    id: root

    property int notifyLeadMinutes: 5
    property int pollIntervalMs: 2000

    // Purely in-memory, fine to lose on restart — worst case a "starting
    // soon" notification fires once more than strictly necessary.
    property var _notifiedToday: ({})
    property int _lastDate: new Date().getDate()

    // No-op — its only job is to be a stable thing to call from
    // shell.qml so this singleton gets instantiated at startup.
    function load() {}

    function _minutesNow(d) {
        return d.getHours() * 60 + d.getMinutes()
    }

    function _resetDedupeIfNewDay(d) {
        if (d.getDate() !== root._lastDate) {
            root._lastDate = d.getDate()
            root._notifiedToday = {}
        }
    }

    function _epochForDateKeyMinute(dateKeyStr, minute) {
        const parts = dateKeyStr.split("-").map(Number)
        const midnight = new Date(parts[0], parts[1] - 1, parts[2], 0, 0, 0, 0)
        return Math.floor(midnight.getTime() / 1000) + minute * 60
    }

    function _metaFor(entry) {
        return {
            "entryId": entry.id, "dateKey": entry.ownerDateKey,
            "startMinute": entry.startMinute, "endMinute": entry.endMinute,
            "label": entry.label, "day": entry.day, "longSession": !!entry.longSession
        }
    }

    function check() {
        // Wait until StudyLog has loaded what's already on disk at least
        // once — otherwise the very first poll right after launch would
        // see an empty `entries` and could re-log something that actually
        // finished before this launch.
        if (!StudyLog.loaded) return

            const now = new Date()
            root._resetDedupeIfNewDay(now)

            const mins = root._minutesNow(now)
            // Today's own blocks, plus the tail of anything that started
            // yesterday and crosses into today. Each entry carries
            // ownerDateKey (the date it actually belongs to / is logged
            // under) and relativeStart/relativeEnd (shifted onto today's
            // 0-1439 clock, negative if it began yesterday) — see
            // StudySchedule.activeEntriesForDate().
            const todays = StudySchedule.activeEntriesForDate(now)

            // ── lead-time warnings ──
            for (const e of todays) {
                if (!e.enabled) continue
                    if (StudyLog.hasCompleted(e.id, e.ownerDateKey)) continue
                        const key = e.id + "-" + e.ownerDateKey
                        if (!root._notifiedToday[key]
                            && mins >= e.relativeStart - root.notifyLeadMinutes
                            && mins < e.relativeStart) {
                            root._notifiedToday[key] = true
                            Quickshell.execDetached([
                                "notify-send", "Study session soon",
                                `"${e.label}" starts in ${e.relativeStart - mins} min`,
                                "-a", "Shell"
                            ])
                            }
            }

            // What SHOULD be driving the pomodoro right now: enabled,
            // in-window (a block that started yesterday and hasn't hit its
            // real end time yet still counts), not already logged complete
            // under the date it actually belongs to.
            let shouldBe = null
            for (const e of todays) {
                if (!e.enabled) continue
                    if (StudyLog.hasCompleted(e.id, e.ownerDateKey)) continue
                        if (mins >= e.relativeStart && mins < e.relativeEnd) { shouldBe = e; break }
            }

            const p = Persistent.states.timer.pomodoro
            const isActivelyDriven = p.scheduleEntryId !== ""
            // Session identity is tracked by the block's OWNER date, not
            // "today" — that's what keeps a session matching itself across
            // a midnight rollover instead of looking like a stale leftover.
            const stillMatches = isActivelyDriven && shouldBe
            && p.scheduleEntryId === shouldBe.id && p.scheduleDateKey === shouldBe.ownerDateKey

            // ── 1. stop a session that's driving but shouldn't be anymore ──
            if (isActivelyDriven && !stillMatches) {
                const was = {
                    "id": p.scheduleEntryId, "dateKey": p.scheduleDateKey,
                    "day": p.scheduleDay, "label": p.scheduleLabel,
                    "startMinute": p.scheduleStartMinute, "endMinute": p.scheduleEndMinute,
                    "longSession": p.scheduleLongSession, "noBreak": p.scheduleNoBreak
                }
                TimerService.endScheduledSession()

                // Log real elapsed time from when the block actually
                // started, not just when it happens to have reached its
                // own scheduled end. Previously this only logged if
                // `nowEpoch >= blockEndEpoch` — so deleting, disabling, or
                // editing the entry even a minute before its scheduled end
                // silently dropped the ENTIRE session with zero minutes
                // credited, no matter how long you'd actually been
                // studying. Now every stopped session gets logged for
                // however long it really ran, capped at the block's own
                // scheduled length so a delayed poll can't overcredit it.
                // Still purely additive and still deduped by id+date, so
                // a session is only ever logged once, and later editing or
                // deleting the schedule entry can't touch or remove what
                // already got appended here.
                const blockStartEpoch = root._epochForDateKeyMinute(was.dateKey, was.startMinute)
                const nowEpoch = Math.floor(now.getTime() / 1000)
                const scheduledMinutes = was.endMinute - was.startMinute
                const elapsedMinutes = Math.max(0, Math.round((nowEpoch - blockStartEpoch) / 60))
                const minutesToLog = Math.min(elapsedMinutes, scheduledMinutes)
                const ranFullLength = minutesToLog >= scheduledMinutes

                if (minutesToLog > 0 && !StudyLog.hasCompleted(was.id, was.dateKey)) {
                    StudyLog.record(was, minutesToLog, was.dateKey, ranFullLength ? "completed" : "stopped-early")
                    Quickshell.execDetached([
                        "notify-send", "Study block done",
                        ranFullLength
                        ? `"${was.label}" has ended · ${StudyLog.formatDuration(minutesToLog)} logged`
                        : `"${was.label}" stopped early · ${StudyLog.formatDuration(minutesToLog)} logged`,
                                            "-a", "Shell"
                    ])
                }
            }

            // ── 2. resync a still-matching session whose own settings changed ──
            if (stillMatches) {
                const focusMinutes = StudySchedule.focusMinutesFor(shouldBe)
                const breakMinutes = StudySchedule.breakMinutes
                const focusSeconds = focusMinutes * 60
                const expectedNoBreak = StudySchedule.expectedNoBreakFor(shouldBe)
                const breakSeconds = expectedNoBreak ? 0 : breakMinutes * 60
                const changed = p.scheduleFocusSeconds !== focusSeconds
                || p.scheduleBreakSeconds !== breakSeconds
                || p.scheduleNoBreak !== expectedNoBreak
                || p.scheduleStartMinute !== shouldBe.startMinute
                || p.scheduleEndMinute !== shouldBe.endMinute

                if (changed) {
                    const blockStartEpochSeconds = root._epochForDateKeyMinute(shouldBe.ownerDateKey, shouldBe.startMinute)
                    TimerService.startScheduledSessionAt(focusSeconds, breakMinutes * 60, expectedNoBreak,
                                                         blockStartEpochSeconds, root._metaFor(shouldBe))
                    Quickshell.execDetached([
                        "notify-send", "Study block updated",
                        `"${shouldBe.label}" resynced to your edits`,
                        "-a", "Shell"
                    ])
                }
            }

            // ── 3. start a session that should be driving but isn't ──
            if (shouldBe && Persistent.states.timer.pomodoro.scheduleEntryId === "") {
                if (!TimerService.pomodoroRunning) {
                    const focusMinutes = StudySchedule.focusMinutesFor(shouldBe)
                    const breakMinutes = StudySchedule.breakMinutes
                    const expectedNoBreak = StudySchedule.expectedNoBreakFor(shouldBe)
                    const blockStartEpochSeconds = root._epochForDateKeyMinute(shouldBe.ownerDateKey, shouldBe.startMinute)
                    TimerService.startScheduledSessionAt(focusMinutes * 60, breakMinutes * 60, expectedNoBreak,
                                                         blockStartEpochSeconds, root._metaFor(shouldBe))
                    Quickshell.execDetached([
                        "notify-send", "Study time",
                        `Starting: ${shouldBe.label}`,
                        "-a", "Shell"
                    ])
                }
                // else: something else (a manual, non-scheduled pomodoro) is
                // already running — deliberately don't interrupt it. We'll
                // pick this block up as soon as that manual session ends.
            }
    }

    Timer {
        interval: root.pollIntervalMs
        running: true
        repeat: true
        triggeredOnStart: true
        onTriggered: root.check()
    }
}

FILE: ./services/SystemInfo.qml

pragma Singleton
pragma ComponentBehavior: Bound

import QtQuick
import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Io

Singleton {
    id: root

    property string distroName: "Unknown"
    property string distroId: "unknown"
    property string distroIcon: ""
    property string username: "user"
    property string hostname: ""
    property string homeUrl: ""
    property string documentationUrl: ""
    property string supportUrl: ""
    property string bugReportUrl: ""
    property string privacyPolicyUrl: ""
    property string logo: ""
    property string desktopEnvironment: ""
    property string windowingSystem: ""
    property string cpu: ""
    property string gpu: ""
    property string memory: ""
    property string disk: ""
    property string shell: ""
    property string packages: ""
    property string installAge: ""
    property string kernelVersion: ""

    function refresh() {
        getCpu.running = false;       getCpu.running = true
        getGpu.running = false;       getGpu.running = true
        getMemory.running = false;    getMemory.running = true
        getDisk.running = false;      getDisk.running = true
        getShell.running = false;     getShell.running = true
        getPackages.running = false;  getPackages.running = true
        getInstallAge.running = false; getInstallAge.running = true
        getKernel.running = false; getKernel.running = true
    }

    function refreshHostname() {
        getHostname.running = false
        getHostname.running = true
    }

    Timer {
        triggeredOnStart: true
        interval: 1
        running: true
        repeat: false
        onTriggered: {
            getUsername.running = true
            getHostname.running = true
            fileOsRelease.reload()
            const textOsRelease = fileOsRelease.text()

            const prettyNameMatch = textOsRelease.match(/^PRETTY_NAME="(.+?)"/m)
            const nameMatch = textOsRelease.match(/^NAME="(.+?)"/m)
            distroName = prettyNameMatch ? prettyNameMatch[1] : (nameMatch ? nameMatch[1].replace(/Linux/i, "").trim() : "Unknown")

            const idMatch = textOsRelease.match(/^ID="?(.+?)"?$/m)
            distroId = idMatch ? idMatch[1] : "unknown"

            const homeUrlMatch = textOsRelease.match(/^HOME_URL="(.+?)"/m)
            homeUrl = homeUrlMatch ? homeUrlMatch[1] : ""
            const documentationUrlMatch = textOsRelease.match(/^DOCUMENTATION_URL="(.+?)"/m)
            documentationUrl = documentationUrlMatch ? documentationUrlMatch[1] : ""
            const supportUrlMatch = textOsRelease.match(/^SUPPORT_URL="(.+?)"/m)
            supportUrl = supportUrlMatch ? supportUrlMatch[1] : ""
            const bugReportUrlMatch = textOsRelease.match(/^BUG_REPORT_URL="(.+?)"/m)
            bugReportUrl = bugReportUrlMatch ? bugReportUrlMatch[1] : ""
            const privacyPolicyUrlMatch = textOsRelease.match(/^PRIVACY_POLICY_URL="(.+?)"/m)
            privacyPolicyUrl = privacyPolicyUrlMatch ? privacyPolicyUrlMatch[1] : ""
            const logoFieldMatch = textOsRelease.match(/^LOGO="?(.+?)"?$/m)
            logo = logoFieldMatch ? logoFieldMatch[1] : ""

            switch (distroId) {
                case "artix":
                case "arch":        distroIcon = "arch-symbolic"; break
                case "endeavouros": distroIcon = "endeavouros-symbolic"; break
                case "cachyos":     distroIcon = "cachyos-symbolic"; break
                case "nixos":       distroIcon = "nixos-symbolic"; break
                case "fedora":      distroIcon = "fedora-symbolic"; break
                case "linuxmint":
                case "ubuntu":
                case "zorin":
                case "popos":       distroIcon = "ubuntu-symbolic"; break
                case "debian":
                case "raspbian":
                case "kali":        distroIcon = "debian-symbolic"; break
                case "funtoo":
                case "gentoo":      distroIcon = "gentoo-symbolic"; break
                default:            distroIcon = "arch-symbolic"; break
            }
            if (textOsRelease.toLowerCase().includes("nyarch"))
                distroIcon = "nyarch-symbolic"

            if (logo.trim().length === 0)
                logo = distroIcon
        }
    }

    Process {
        id: getUsername
        command: ["whoami"]
        stdout: SplitParser { onRead: data => root.username = data.trim() }
    }

    Process {
        id: getHostname
        command: ["cat", "/etc/hostname"]
        stdout: SplitParser { onRead: data => root.hostname = data.trim() }
    }

    Process {
        id: getDesktopEnvironment
        running: true
        command: ["bash", "-c", "echo $XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP,$WAYLAND_DISPLAY"]
        stdout: StdioCollector {
            id: deCollector
            onStreamFinished: {
                const [desktop, wayland] = deCollector.text.split(",")
                root.desktopEnvironment = desktop.trim()
                root.windowingSystem = wayland.trim().length > 0 ? "Wayland" : "X11"
            }
        }
    }

    FileView {
        id: fileOsRelease
        path: "/etc/os-release"
    }

    Process {
        id: getKernel
        running: false
        command: ["uname", "-r"]
        stdout: SplitParser { onRead: data => root.kernelVersion = data.trim() }
    }

    Process {
        id: getCpu
        running: false
        command: ["bash", "-c", "grep -m1 'model name' /proc/cpuinfo | cut -d':' -f2- | sed 's/^ //' | sed 's/Intel(R)/Intel®/' | sed 's/Core(TM)/Core™/' | sed 's/CPU //' | sed 's/  */ /g' | sed 's/ @ */ @/'"]
        stdout: SplitParser { onRead: data => root.cpu = data.trim() }
    }

    Process {
        id: getGpu
        running: false
        command: ["bash", "-c", `
            gpu=$(glxinfo 2>/dev/null | grep 'renderer string' | grep -o 'Intel(R) HD Graphics [0-9]\\{4\\}' | sed 's/Intel(R)/Intel®/')
            if [ -z "$gpu" ]; then
                gpu=$(lspci | grep -iE 'vga|3d|display' | head -1 | sed -E '
                    s/.*: //;
                    s/\\(rev [0-9a-f]+\\)//;
                    s/Advanced Micro Devices, Inc\\. \\[AMD\\/ATI\\]//;
                    s/NVIDIA Corporation//;
                    s/Intel Corporation//;
                    s/.*\\[([^]]+)\\]$/\\1/;
                    s/^ *//;
                    s/ *$//
                ')
            fi
            echo "$gpu"
        `]
        stdout: SplitParser { onRead: data => root.gpu = data.trim() }
    }

    Process {
        id: getMemory
        running: false
        command: ["bash", "-c", "LC_ALL=C free -h | awk '/^Mem:/ {print $3 \" / \" $2}'"]
        stdout: SplitParser { onRead: data => root.memory = data.trim() }
    }

    Process {
        id: getDisk
        running: false
        command: ["bash", "-c", "df -h / | awk 'NR==2 {print $3 \" / \" $2}'"]
        stdout: SplitParser { onRead: data => root.disk = data.trim() }
    }

    Process {
        id: getShell
        running: false
        command: ["bash", "-c", "echo $SHELL | awk -F'/' '{print $NF}'"]
        stdout: SplitParser { onRead: data => root.shell = data.trim() }
    }

    Process {
        id: getPackages
        running: false
        command: ["bash", "-c", "pacman_count=$(pacman -Q | wc -l); flatpak_count=$(flatpak list 2>/dev/null | wc -l || echo 0); if [ \"$flatpak_count\" -gt 0 ]; then echo \"$pacman_count pacman, $flatpak_count fp\"; else echo \"$pacman_count pacman\"; fi"]
        stdout: SplitParser { onRead: data => root.packages = data.trim() }
    }

    Process {
        id: getInstallAge
        running: false
        command: ["bash", "-c", "install_sec=$(stat -c %W /); if [ \"$install_sec\" -le 0 ]; then install_sec=$(stat -c %Y /); fi; now_sec=$(date +%s); age_sec=$((now_sec - install_sec)); days=$((age_sec / 86400)); echo \"$days days\""]
        stdout: SplitParser { onRead: data => root.installAge = data.trim() }
    }
}
